readerContract.humanQuestion: If I am building a personal site/app or coordinating a larger work project, what does Cursor Projects actually change, and what still needs my review?
readerContract.promisedPayoff: Explain the stated coordinator, cloud/local handoff, shared context, beta rollout, and lack of a quality guarantee.
readerContract.priorKnowledge: A reader may know an AI chat can help on one task but not how multiple agents can persist across a job.
readerContract.centralMentalModel: A Project is a continuing job folder: a coordinator plans and delegates, cloud work continues after the laptop closes, and local testing can use a local agent.
readerContract.dailyLifeConnection: A personal site/app build or a larger work project can involve several connected tasks and pauses between laptop sessions.
readerContract.surfaceJob: A short sourced NewsStand notice that makes the new beta’s mechanism and limits legible without telling every reader they need it.
readerContract.desiredFeeling: Clear enough to judge whether the release is relevant, without overpromising.

canonicalTruth.freshnessTrigger: Any Cursor revision to Projects availability, coordinator behavior, cloud/local execution, or shared context.

readerQuestions.question: What is Cursor Projects and who may find it relevant?
What happens when the laptop closes or local testing is needed?
What does the release not promise?

requiredTerms.reason: The term is necessary to explain who plans and delegates work.

draftArchitecture.plainAnswer: Cursor Projects is a beta for longer AI-assisted jobs, where a coordinator plans and delegates work while finished work returns to the reader to check.
draftArchitecture.workedCase: A reader building a personal website/app can see why a continuing Project differs from starting a new chat after each laptop session.
draftArchitecture.transferCase: A reader coordinating a larger work project can ask whether its job has an inspectable result before relying on a continuing agent workflow.
draftArchitecture.usefulAction: Use the article’s practical question—whether the job is bounded and inspectable—rather than assuming a beta can finish everything.
draftArchitecture.formatSpecificStructure: Dated release, plain coordinator definition, cloud/local mechanism, reader relevance and limits, then concise takeaway.
draftArchitecture.antiTemplateDecision: No stock productivity promise, price speculation, or decorative analogy; the story stays with the stated handoff and review boundary.
causalSequence: A Project retains context for a larger body of work.
The coordinator plans and delegates rather than writing code itself.
Cloud work can continue after the laptop closes, while machine-specific testing calls a local agent.
Finished work returns to the reader to check.

humourPlan.noneReason: The release needs a plain mechanism and boundary in a short notice; humour would not teach either.

communicationDesign.surfaceAdaptation: This short notice begins with the reader’s decision, makes the coordinator/cloud/local sequence visible, and keeps provider-only limits.

humanQuestion.reason: Readers need to know whether a longer agent workflow changes their project choice.
humanQuestion.plannedEvidence: The useful question is whether you have a bounded job that can continue while your laptop is closed and that you can inspect when it returns.

usefulCuriosity.reason: A delayed reveal would not help this short news notice.

invisibleProcessConcrete.reason: Planning, cloud continuation and local testing are otherwise invisible.
invisibleProcessConcrete.plannedEvidence: A Project runs on a cloud computer... Cursor says the coordinator starts a local agent.

familiarTechnicalMovement.reason: Personal site/app and larger work project cases return to the coordinator mechanism.
familiarTechnicalMovement.plannedEvidence: That could suit a personal website or app, or a work project.

limitationsConsequences.reason: Vendor claims alone do not prove a quality outcome.
limitationsConsequences.plannedEvidence: It is not a promise that the result will be right.

betterNextQuestion.reason: The reader needs a bounded decision test.
betterNextQuestion.plannedEvidence: whether you have a bounded job that can continue while your laptop is closed and that you can inspect when it returns.

explanationArc.adaptation: The article answers a current release question in under 300 words rather than using a substantial lesson arc.

representativeProofPlan.highestRisk: The article could make a cloud/local workflow sound like autonomous quality or universal suitability.
representativeProofPlan.plannedProof: Exact source excerpts bind release assertions; source budget counts every visible field; producer review checks the review boundary and translation spans.
representativeProofPlan.acceptanceOutcome: A reader can state what continues in the cloud, when a local agent is used, and why finished work still needs checking.
